findings.F1: Obligation example 'You must hand in your homework by Friday.' sits under the deduction sense
findings.F2: Usage note uses the banned abbreviation 'e.g.'
findings.F3: The no-past/had to and mustn't versus don't have to facts are repeated across the explanation, usage note, learner errors and grammar adaptation
findings.F4: The cannot/can't opposite of deductive must is stated in the explanation, the compare note and the semantic adaptation
findings.F5: shall-modal listed as a synonym of obligation must, though that use is formal or legal
findings.F6: have-v is linked in both compare and see_also, saying the same thing
findings.F7: Sense 1 pattern 'verb + to-infinitive' is wrong; must takes a bare infinitive
findings.F8: The fixed use 'I must say' / 'I must admit' is not covered
